title: Bond order of dioxygen and its ions
body: A student uses molecular orbital theory to compare dioxygen and the ions formed from it. For O2 (16 electrons) the configuration is KK (sigma2s)2 (sigma*2s)2 (sigma2pz)2 (pi2px)2 (pi2py)2 (pi*2px)1 (pi*2py)1. The bond order is given by (1/2)(Nb - Na), where Nb and Na are the numbers of electrons in bonding and antibonding orbitals. A higher bond order means a stronger bond, a larger bond dissociation enthalpy and a shorter bond, while a bond order of zero means the molecule is not expected to exist. Removing an electron from O2 takes it out of a pi* orbital, giving O2+; adding one or two electrons places them in the pi* orbitals, giving the superoxide ion O2- and the peroxide ion O2(2-).
